new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and falls on the syllable with a (phonetically) long vowel, which in this variety is the closed syllable; i.e. prominence tracks vowel length/closed-syllable weight rather than a fixed position. The companion Nagpuria sketch in the same volume (p. 459) says the same thing the other way round: syllables with long vocoids are always stressed, and length is predictable (monosyllables long; second syllable long in longer words).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a phoneme-inventory sketch of Jharkhand Sadan/Sadri (sadr1248); no data on phrases or citation forms. Applies to Bangladesh Oraon Sadri (orao1237) only by extension; no source describes Oraon Sadri phonology.
new_statements.identity_note: No phonological or grammatical description of Oraon Sadri (orao1237, the Sadri of the Oraon/Kurukh diaspora in NW Bangladesh; Glottolog 5.1 lists 0 descriptive refs, OLAC lists only Glottolog and Ethnologue) could be found. The stress statement quoted below is a PROXY: it describes Sadan/Sadri of Jharkhand = Sadri [sck] sadr1248 (LSI Jharkhand 2023), the parent variety from which Bangladesh Oraon Sadri descends; Glottolog/Ethnologue split sdr from sck on the basis of unpublished SIL Bangladesh survey data, not on any published phonology. The same volume's Nagpuria chapter (also sadr1248) gives a compatible statement (p. 459: syllables with long vocoids are always stressed). Das & Raha 1963 (the one Glottolog ref with a language chapter, on Sunderban Oraons in West Bengal) describes their Sadri as a Hindi-Bengali mixture with sample texts only; no phonology. Reviewer must decide whether a sister-code source is admissible for orao1237; I have not marked it a catalog candidate.
